Concise Clinical Note

Consult Summary:
Adult male with 4-day viral prodrome (sore throat → rhinorrhea/nasal congestion → new dry cough) with mild systemic symptoms; impression most consistent with viral upper respiratory tract infection/early influenza‐like illness.

History:
• Presenting complaint: “Under the weather” × 4 days.  
• Timeline:  
  – Day 0: Sore throat with odynophagia, low-grade fever.  
  – Days 1-2: Rhinorrhea (clear) and nasal congestion, sore throat improving.  
  – Day 3 (yesterday): Onset of persistent dry cough.  
  – Ongoing: Night sweats, fatigue, intermittent generalized headache, new myalgias, mild exertional dyspnea (none at rest).  
• Pertinent negatives: No chest pain, no ear pain/discharge, no visual changes, no photophobia, no nausea/vomiting, no rash, bowels and urine normal.  
• Past medical history: Denies chronic illnesses.  
• Allergies: None known.  
• Medications: Paracetamol and ibuprofen as needed for fever/pain.  
• Family history: Grandmother—type 2 DM; great-grandfather—eczema.  
• Social / preventive: Lives alone; accountant; occasional cigar use; social alcohol; work stress but mood stable; no regular exercise currently due to illness.

Examination:
Telehealth visit—no vitals or direct physical findings available.

Impression:
Most likely:  
1. Viral upper respiratory tract infection (common cold) – classic symptom progression, self-limiting course, improving fever.  
Possible alternatives:  
2. Influenza – systemic symptoms (myalgias, headache, night sweats) but fever short-lived.  
3. Mild COVID-19 – overlapping features and exposure history; less likely given rapid improvement and no anosmia.

Plan:
• Supportive care: Rest, increased oral fluids.  
• Medications: Continue paracetamol and/or ibuprofen as needed for fever, sore throat, myalgias.  
• Activity: Take 1–2 days off work.  
• Red-flag advice: Return sooner for high or persistent fever, worsening breathlessness, chest pain, or if symptoms last > 7 days without improvement.  
• Follow-up: Routine re-evaluation next week if not resolving.

Quality checks:

● Missing expected elements: vital signs, physical examination, immunization status (e.g., flu/COVID vaccines), COVID testing history.  
● Conflicts: None noted between transcript and DDx.  
● Transcript quality: Clear history; no objective exam or vitals due to telehealth format; otherwise coherent.
